body:
The author mentioned cannabis and barbiturates as additional substances when submitting this report, but they are not mentioned in the report itself. The death mentioned below has not been verified.
When I was 14 years old, I met my best friend and soul mate.  We were not lovers, but our connection was unbreakable.  We would spend every waking hour together.  Now, the only time I get to see him is if I take a trip to out small town cemetery and look at his headstone.
When we first met, he had just began smoking weed, and it was something that had interested me immensly, so I decided that I would also try it.  It was no big deal, and to this day, I will still condone it.  But within my group of friends, as much as we hate to admit it, it was the epitome of a gateway drug.  We began to experiment with acid, which, like the weed, was not a big issue and didn't seem to pose any risks.  Then it was X, and we were extremely careful.  We did our research, and always took all the proper precautions.  Those few things were what we stuck to, never straying into the intimidating world of 'hard-core' drugs.  Or so I thought.
One day I discovered I was wrong about this avoidance, when I over heard my soul-mate talking about heroin with a girl I thought to be in 'the wrong crowd.'  I was always against that drug, so right there in the hallway of our little high school, I told him how I felt about it, and that I would not let him do it.  He looked me in the eyes and promised not to.
Later that night, my now fiance and I took some rolls while my parents were out of town.  It was going beautifully.  Then my friend returned from a party, and came over to hang out for a little while.  He was acting kind of strange, but I assumed it was just from the Opium.  We hung out, and then my fiance went inside the house.  I gave my friend a hug, and he told me he was going home to crash.  Little did I know, at that moment, I would be the last person to see him alive.
Apparently, he had bought 2 'boys,' they called them, of heroin.  He went home, prepared himself to get high, and then snorted the first line.  I know this only because he had been writing a detailed account of his experimentation on his computer as this occured.  He said he felt pretty good, but a little dizzy and itchy.  He decided to go for the other packet.  At that point he was feeling marvelous, but nauseous, so he decided to lay down on his bed.  At that point, his body seized up, and though he was consious, he could not move.  He was lying on his back and began to vomit.  He aspyrated, suffocated, and then his heart stopped.
I got a call around 10:30 the next morning from my fiance's sister ...'R's heart stopped, he's at the hospital, you need to go pick up B.'  It was the most sobering moment of my life.  I believe at that moment, my heart stopped, too.  The drive to the hospital was frantic and reckless.  When we arrived, we waited, and waited, and I was in the bathroom puking because the thought of all of this made me so sick.  The ER doctor informed us that he would have to be Care-Flighted to a hospital 40 minutes away because they didn't have the resources to save him.  I went outside on this gorgeous May day, and prayed, while sobbing, with my friend's mother.  I'm an atheist, but I prayed anyway.  The moment that sticks with me the most, out of all this craziness, was when the paramedics rushed his near lifeless body outside, directly in front of me (those 15 seconds seemed to last 15 years), and loaded his gurney into the intensely loud 'helicopter of life.'
He lasted for 3 days on life support, with decreasing brain activity.  I went to say goodbye to him, along with his ever loyal girlfriend, parents, and 7 year old little sister, and he died.  The machines stopped, and the room was silent.  I got one chance to kiss his forehead before I broke down on the floor, clutching his baby sister in my arms. Our hearts broke together.
I have only good memories of him, so I was lucky.  His last words still resound in my head every time I think of this.  All that comes to mind when I think about losing my shining star...'I told him not too.'  And I wish that was enough.
Though this account is lengthy, I hope it helps make some life changing decisions.
